guardian.description:
Eighteen children among the people killed after ferry capsized on Lake Kariba

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

Serving in Mission International said Kevin Rideout “is in good health in the care of US officials” and would soon be reunited with his extended family.

guardian.description:
Quake struck Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground for fear of a tsunami

A 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia has killed at least 47 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly seismic events.

Rescuers have yet to reach Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, because roads were blocked by landslides and communications disrupted.

Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre

Orangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out in Indonesia in recent weeks.

Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.

rfi.title: Europe's shrinking rivers give rise to debate over how to tackle drought
rfi.description: Europe's shrinking rivers are disrupting industry, reducing power generation and intensifying the debate over how to respond to worsening drought. As water levels fall across the continent, authorities and businesses alike are looking for ways to keep freight moving and critical infrastructure operating. Hydrologists warn, however, that digging rivers deeper cannot create more water and could make shortages worse.

rfi.title: Armenian Genocide survivors' grandson says 'political motives' block recognition
rfi.description: In 1915, the Ottoman Empire began the systematic deportation and massacre of its Armenian population. As many as 1.5 million Armenians were killed – widely regarded by historians as the twentieth century's first genocide, and the event for which the term was later coined. Stephan Pechdimaldji, the grandson of two of the survivors, spoke to RFI about why recognition still matters.

rfi.title: Nine killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon as tensions test peace framework
rfi.description: At least nine people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to Lebanon’s state news agency, in some of the deadliest attacks since Beirut agreed to a US-mediated framework aimed at ending the latest round of fighting.

rfi.title: France's successive heatwaves show strain of living in urban 'heat islands'
rfi.description: As France experiences its latest heatwave, residents of urban "heat islands" – dense neighbourhoods with few trees or green spaces – are suffering acutely in the high temperatures, and local authorities are searching for solutions.

rfi.title: France probes unprecedented cyberattack after tax data of 678,000 users stolen
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a major cyberattack on the country’s tax administration that affected nearly 700,000 individuals and businesses, authorities said on Saturday.

rfi.title: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghanistan seeks to ease international isolation
rfi.description: In the five years since the Taliban seized back power in Afghanistan, the country's worsening human rights record has drawn sanctions and aid cuts. But despite refusing to officially recognise the fundamentalist movement's government, some countries are concluding that engaging with the Taliban has become unavoidable.

rfi.title: In Turkey, one of the world's longest conflicts reaches a turning point
rfi.description: Turkey stands on the threshold of closing a conflict spanning almost 50 years, after the Turkish parliament this week passed a law allowing exiled Kurdish militants to return home and rejoin society. The legislation aims to end the war with the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which has battled the Turkish state for independence since 1984.

rfi.title: Law on assisted dying wins constitutional approval in France
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council on Friday approved a law creating a right to assisted dying, removing the last major legal obstacle before the measure can be enacted and implemented.

rfi.title: Fake accounts and false rumours drive new Ceuta crossing campaign
rfi.description: Calls for a new mass crossing into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on Morocco's Mediterranean coast, have flooded Moroccan social media, with posts urging migrants to rush the border on Saturday. An RFI investigation found the campaign was fuelled by false rumours, suspicious accounts and signs of artificial amplification.

rfi.title: US missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after more than nine months
rfi.description: American Kevin Rideout, who worked as a pilot for an evangelical organisation, has been freed after he was kidnapped in October 2025 in Niamey. His release comes as the security situation remains tense in Niger.

rfi.title: Top French court scraps social media ban for children under 15
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council struck down a law on Friday that would have banned children under 15 from using social media from September. The judges ruled that the measure placed a disproportionate restriction on freedom of expression and communication.

rfi.title: French firefighters threaten to strike over lack of resources
rfi.description: As wildfires continue to burn across France, representatives of firefighters' unions said they would go on strike in September to protest a lack of resources. Despite a meeting with the interior minister on Thursday, they say they are unhappy with the government's response so far.

rfi.title: Farage wins UK by-election as Count Binface claims 'moral victory'

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : le jeu trouble de l’Elysée, qui agite l’hypothèse Lecornu
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Etat, omniprésent, n’a pas l’intention de s’effacer à l’approche de la présidentielle. Alors que les deux candidats déclarés du bloc central, Edouard Philippe et Gabriel Attal, sont insatisfaisants à ses yeux, sa garde rapprochée pousse l’hypothèse de la candidature du premier ministre.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies et canicule : 28 départements de l’est de la France en vigilance orange ; dans les Landes, pas de « reprise majeure » du feu au cours des dernières heures
lemonde.description: La situation évolue « plutôt favorablement » dans les Landes, où l’incendie qui s’est déclaré jeudi à Luglon n’a pas connu de « reprise majeure » dans la nuit, a annoncé le préfet dimanche matin, tout en excluant un retour prochain des 650 personnes évacuées.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : au moins trois blessés à Kiev après une attaque de missiles ; Moscou visée par 600 drones pendant la nuit
lemonde.description: A Kryvy Rih, dans le centre de l’Ukraine, une personne a été tuée et six autres blessées. Par ailleurs, Moscou a été visée par 600 drones pendant la nuit, une attaque d’une rare ampleur qui a fait au moins trois blessés, selon le maire de la capitale russe.

lemonde.title: « Les luttes de faction à Téhéran pèsent sur les pourparlers avec les Etats-Unis »
lemonde.description: Les gardiens de la révolution ne contrôlent pas seulement les opérations militaires, ils imposent aussi leurs exigences au président iranien et à ses négociateurs, analyse l’historien Jean-Pierre Filiu dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: Championnats d’Europe de natation 2026 : Mary-Ambre Moluh, sacrée sur le 100 m dos, poursuit sa belle lancée vers les Jeux 2028
lemonde.description: La Francilienne de 20 ans s’est offert une nouvelle médaille dans la compétition, samedi, quelques jours après s’être adjugé l’or sur le relais 4 × 100 m quatre nages mixte et l’argent sur le 50 m dos. Sa compatriote Pauline Mahieu est en bronze.

lemonde.title: L’autrice Emma Becker racontée par son clan : « Elle a appris l’érotisme dans notre bibliothèque ! »
lemonde.description: « Un écrivain dans la famille » (6/6). Qu’elle décrive son expérience de la prostitution à Berlin dans « La Maison », ou sa torride relation extraconjugale dans « Le Mal joli », Emma Becker a pris le parti, depuis ses débuts, de se raconter sur un mode érotique, dans des récits où ses proches ont toute leur place. Une mise à nu souvent crue, dont l’entourage de l’autrice salue la liberté.

lemonde.title: Un premier porte-conteneurs chinois, le « Dubai Tower », a pris la route de l’Europe via l’Arctique
lemonde.description: Ce voyage inaugural, qui doit être hebdomadaire, s’inscrit dans le projet chinois de « route de la soie polaire » et permet d’éviter une région Proche-Moyen-Orient de plus en plus instable.

lemonde.title: Au Japon, les pluies diluviennes près de Tokyo causent la mort d’au moins neuf personnes
lemonde.description: Dès vendredi matin, le cumul sur la ville de Chiba dépassait de plus de trois fois le total de précipitations habituel pour un mois d’août entier, d’après le ministère des territoires. Selon les scientifiques, le réchauffement climatique engendré par l’activité humaine rend ce type de phénomène extrême plus fréquent, plus long et plus intense.

lemonde.title: « Les questions que pose une famille qui veut s’installer, c’est : “Où est l’école et où peut-on se faire soigner ?” » : dans les Vosges, les maires essaient d’attirer les jeunes couples

lemonde.title: « Et, au fait, qui sait où est la pompe du paddle ? » : l’été à un accessoire près
lemonde.description: « Les douleurs des vacances » (5/7). Tous les ans c’est la même histoire. Une roue de vélo dégonflée sans pompe, une tente sans sardines ou encore des raquettes sans balles. Et pourtant, ces objets restent dans les garages. Pourquoi est-ce si difficile de s’en séparer ?

lemonde.title: Fortes pluies et coupures de courant : l’ouragan Lala menace Hawaï

lemonde.title: Championnats d’Europe d’athlétisme : Jimmy Gressier décroche la médaille de bronze du 10 000 m
lemonde.description: Le Français, champion du monde de la discipline, n’a rien pu faire face au Suédois Andreas Almgren, facile vainqueur, samedi, mais s’adjuge tout de même, à 29 ans, le premier podium continental de sa carrière.

france24fr.description: Entré dans l'espace aérien roumain près des frontières avec l'Ukraine et la Moldavie, un drone a été abattu dimanche par un avion de combat espagnol en mission dans ce pays de l'Otan, selon le ministre roumain de la Défense. La Roumanie est l'un des États les plus exposés aux conséquences de la guerre en Ukraine parmi les membres de l'Alliance atlantique.

france24fr.title: Séisme en Indonésie : au moins 48 morts, des milliers d'évacués en attente d'aide
france24fr.description: Au lendemain du puissant séisme qui a secoué l'île indonésienne de Florès, des milliers de personnes évacuées attendent de l'aide, dimanche, poussés hors de chez eux la veille par une forte secousse de magnitude 7,7 qui a fait au moins 48 morts et des dizaines de blessés. Les habitants de certaines régions sont sans électricité ni accès aux télécommunications, et au moins une route d'accès d'urgence reste impraticable.

france24fr.title: De 80 à 2 700 hectares brûlés en 24 heures : la Belgique face à l'un des pires feux de son histoire
france24fr.description: La Belgique combat l'un des pires incendies de son histoire. Le brasier ravageait, samedi encore, les Fagnes, une grande réserve boisée du pays, prisée des randonneurs et proche de l'Allemagne. De 80 hectares brûlés vendredi, il a bondi à plus de 2 700 samedi soir, selon un communiqué des autorités locales. De premiers habitants dans deux villages ont reçu l'ordre d'évacuer.

france24fr.title: La Colombie demande à Trump de suspendre les droits de douane après le séisme meurtrier
france24fr.description: Le président de la Colombie, Abelardo de la Espriella, tout juste entré en fonction, a demandé samedi à Donald Trump une suspension des droits de douanes pour aider la reconstruction, après le tremblement de terre qui a fait près de 300 morts. Les droits de douane des États-Unis sur les produits colombiens sont passés de 10 % à 12,5 % fin juillet, à l'exception de certains produits comme le café ou le pétrole.

france24fr.title: Après la Supercoupe d'Europe, le PSG lorgne sur le Trophée des champions
france24fr.description: Après la Supercoupe d'Europe mercredi, le Paris SG a déjà l'occasion d'empocher son deuxième titre de la saison lors du Trophée des champions dimanche soir à Lens, au stade Bollaert-Delelis. En mai, le dernier match entre les deux formations a été remporté par Paris-SG. Le coup d'envoi sera donné à 20 h 45.

france24fr.title: Une inondation dans le nord-ouest de l'Espagne fait deux morts, deux bébés blessés
france24fr.description: Deux femmes ont été tuées samedi dans une inondation et un glissement de terrain dans le nord-ouest de l'Espagne, ont annoncé les services d'urgences régionaux, ajoutant que deux bébés ont été blessés.

france24fr.title: Ukraine en direct : des explosions retentissent à Kiev, Moscou visée par 600 drones
france24fr.description: Des explosions ont retenti à Kiev dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche après le déclenchement d'une alerte aux missiles balistiques dans la capitale ukrainienne, a constaté une journaliste de l'AFP. De son côté, Moscou a été visée par 600 drones, une attaque d'une rare ampleur qui a fait au moins trois blessés, a indiqué le maire de la capitale russe. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Son contrôle judiciaire assoupli, Patrick Bruel est autorisé à quitter le territoire français
france24fr.description: Le contrôle judiciaire de Patrick Bruel, mis en examen pour viol et agression sexuelle, a été assoupli, l'autorisant à quitter le territoire français, a déclaré samedi le parquet de Nanterre. Ce dernier a indiqué avoir fait appel de cette décision.

france24fr.title: L'opposant Succès Masra s'exprime sur France 24 le lendemain de sa libération
france24fr.description: Au Tchad, Succès Masra est désormais libre. L’ancien Premier ministre et opposant, condamné à 20 ans de prison, a bénéficié d’une grâce présidentielle. Ce soir, sa première interview depuis sa libération.

france24fr.title: Léon Marchand remporte son premier titre européen sur le 200 m papillon
Championnats d'Europe de natation : une soirée dorée pour Léon Marchand et Mary-Ambre Moluh
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France de natation a remporté deux titres, samedi à domicile, lors des championnats d'Europe. Le champion olympique Léon Marchand a raflé son premier titre européen en arrivant premier au 200 m papillon, signant la meilleure performance mondiale de l'année. Sacrée au 100 m dos, Mary-Ambre Moluh a, elle, amélioré son propre record d'Europe.

france24fr.title: Après le piratage du fisc, le parquet de Paris ouvre une enquête
france24fr.description: Le parquet de Paris a annoncé samedi avoir ouvert une enquête après la cyberattaque ayant permis fin juin à des pirates de voler les données personnelles de près de 700 000 usagers de l'administration fiscale. Pour les particuliers, ces données concernent notamment les noms et prénoms, le quotient familial, le revenu fiscal de référence et le taux de prélèvement à la source.

france24fr.title: Le président sud-coréen propose des discussions à Pyongyang pour mettre fin à la guerre de Corée
france24fr.description: À l'opposé de la ligne très dure adoptée par son prédécesseur vis-à-vis de Pyongyang, le président sud-coréen Lee Jae-myung a proposé samedi à la Corée du Nord d'entamer un dialogue pour mettre formellement fin à la guerre de Corée, commencée en 1950 et qui n'est toujours pas officiellement terminée, faute de traité de paix.

france24fr.title: Cinq ans après le retour des Taliban : les Afghanes toujours exclues de la société
france24fr.description: Cinq ans après la reprise de Kaboul par les Taliban, quelle est la situation en Afghanistan ? Le retour à une sécurité relative qui exclut la moitié de la population. Plus d'une centaine de décrets ont été adoptés par le nouveau régime pour restreindre les droits des femmes : apparence, éducation, circulation, travail. Décryptage avec Mélina Huet, grand reporter pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Afghanistan : pourquoi la communauté internationale s'accommode des Taliban ?
france24fr.description: Cinq ans après la reprise de Kaboul par les Taliban, quelle est la situation en Afghanistan ? Le retour à une sécurité relative qui exclut la moitié de la population. france24fr.title: Le triangle des Bermudes : un mystère pas si mystérieux que ça
france24fr.description: Disparitions mystérieuses, navires découverts abandonnés... Le triangle des Bermudes est considéré par certains comme la zone la plus dangereuse du monde. Mais mérite-t-elle vraiment cette réputation ?

france24fr.title: Loi sur l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux mineurs : le conseil constitutionnel censure
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a chargé Sébastien Lecornu de "travailler" à "une rédaction juridiquement robuste" de l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans dont la version adoptée au Parlement a été censurée jeudi par le Conseil constitutionnel.

zeit.description: Sie träumen von Ihrer eigenen Insel? Kürzlich wurde in Hamburg eine versteigert, leider eine Ruine. Was haben die neuen Besitzer damit vor?

Mousse de Maracuyá: Kühlschrank auf, Fernweh weg

zeit.description: Nach Berechnungen des IW haben deutsche Unternehmen ihre Direktinvestitionen in den USA um 65 Prozent gesenkt. Der Negativtrend begann mit Trumps zweiter Amtszeit.

spiegel.title: Nationalparks in den USA: Yosemite erlebt Verkehrschaos und Personalmangel
spiegel.description: Ranger abgezogen, Wiesen als Parkplatz, Tausende Autos im Stau: Seit Trumps Kurswechsel spielen sich im US-Naturparadies chaotische Szenen ab.

spiegel.title: Reifenteile auf dem Rollfeld, manövrierunfähige Maschine – Betrieb am Münchner Flughafen wieder normal
spiegel.description: Kurz nach dem Start in München musste ein Flugzeug dort gleich wieder landen, es kam zu Verspätungen. Nun läuft der Betrieb am Flughafen wieder ohne Einschränkungen. Weiterhin sind die Ursachen jedoch noch unklar.

spiegel.title: Jane Seymour: Schauspielerin erinnert sich an ihre »schrecklichste« Bond-Szene
spiegel.description: Ihren Durchbruch hatte sie als Bond-Girl. Nun spricht Schauspielerin Jane Seymour über eine Szene in »Leben und sterben lassen«, die der »reinste Horror« gewesen sei – und erklärt, warum man sie überhaupt engagiert habe.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Bus aus Polen verunglückt – zwölf Tote und viele Verletzte
spiegel.description: Im Osten Ungarns ist ein Bus von der Straße abgekommen und schwer verunglückt. Neben den 57 Fahrgästen waren zwei Fahrer an Bord – einer wurde von der Polizei in Gewahrsam genommen.

spiegel.title: Cannabis-Gesetz: Drogenfahnder kritisiert Folgen der Teilentkriminalisierung
spiegel.description: Vor zwei Jahren wurde der Besitz von Gras teilweise entkriminalisiert. Hier spricht der Drogenfahnder Ingo Hörmann über die Folgen der Legalisierung und darüber, warum er selbst Großdealer wieder laufen lassen muss.

spiegel.title: Nordrhein-Westfalen: Bürger in Monschau sollen bis 10 Uhr Häuser verlassen
spiegel.description: Aufgrund der Ausbreitung eines Brands in Belgien sollen Bürgerinnen und Bürger einiger Ortsteile der nordrhein-westfälischen Stadt Monschau ihre Häuser räumen. Die Rauchbelastung könnte gesundheitsgefährdend sein.

spiegel.title: Willi Buisson, Ex-Vorstandsmitglied des FC Bayern München: Aktiver Widerstand gegen Hitler
spiegel.description: Willi Buisson, ehemaliges Vorstandsmitglied des FC Bayern, wurde 1940 wegen Landesverrats hingerichtet. Eine neue Biografie zeichnet sein abenteuerliches Leben nach.

spiegel.title: Volksbad-Aktion für Schwarze: Warum die Absage so bitter ist – Meinung
spiegel.description: Für ein paar Stunden sollen keine Weißen ins Pop-up-Schwimmbad der Berliner Volksbühne. Die Debatte darüber läuft so heiß, dass die Aktion wegen Sicherheitsbedenken abgesagt werden muss. Das ist bitter – und gute Kunst.

spiegel.title: Kairo: Eine Palästinenserin eröffnet ein Restaurant für ihre Heimat - nur gute Nachrichten
spiegel.description: Eine Palästinenserin bringt ihre Heimat nach Kairo. Dem größten Korallenriff der Welt geht es besser. Und: Hunde mögen Ihr Lächeln. Die guten Nachrichten der Woche.

spiegel.title: Rumänien: Nato-Kampfjet schießt Drohne ab
spiegel.description: Ein spanisches Kampfflugzeug hat nach Angaben der rumänischen Regierung eine Drohne im Luftraum des Landes nahe der Grenze zur Ukraine abgefangen. Das Verteidigungsministerium machte keine Angaben zur Herkunft der Drohne.

spiegel.title: Abba: 50 Jahre »Dancing Queen« – wie gut kennen Sie das Lied? SPIEGEL-Musikquiz
spiegel.description: »You can dance, you can jive, having the time of your life«: Den Ohrwurm hätten Sie jetzt schon mal. Aber was wissen Sie sonst über Abbas »Dancing Queen«? Machen Sie den Test zum fünfzigjährigen Jubiläum des Songs.

spiegel.title: Rätsel der Woche: Zwei Seitenlängen gesucht
spiegel.description: Bei einem rechtwinkligen Dreieck entsprechen alle drei Seitenlängen natürlichen Zahlen. Wir kennen die Länge einer Kathete. Wie lang sind dann die beiden anderen Seiten?

spiegel.title: »Minecraft«: Platz 2 im SPIEGEL Games-Kanon
spiegel.description: »Minecraft« ist unendliche Spielwiese und libertäres Projekt. Denn in diesem Land aus Blöcken kann jeder tun und lassen, was er will.

spiegel.title: »Ex on the Beach«: Ist Brenda Brinkmann so toxisch wie Aleks Petrović?
Hitze und Niedrigwasser: Neuer SPD-Klima-Aktionsplan fordert die Union heraus
spiegel.description: Als Reaktion auf Hitze und Niedrigwasser stellen die SPD-Bundesminister einen Aktionsplan auf. Darin beharren sie darauf, das Grundgesetz für Klimaanpassungen zu ändern. Auch wenn die Union das gerade abgelehnt hat.

spiegel.title: Gerti Tetzner: Der unterdrückte DDR-Roman erscheint erstmals
spiegel.description: Vor mehr als 40 Jahren klopfte die Stasi an die Tür einer Schriftstellerin. Ihr Buch erschien nie. Sie hörte auf zu schreiben. Jetzt kann man den Roman endlich lesen. Ein Gespräch mit Gerti Tetzner übers Aufhören, Anfangen und über das, was dazwischen passiert.

spiegel.title: US-Nationalparks: Donald Trumps Kulturkampf gegen Amerikas Naturparadiese
spiegel.description: Yosemite, Yellowstone, Grand Canyon: Die amerikanischen Nationalparks sind Sehnsuchtsorte für Millionen Menschen aus der ganzen Welt. Nun geraten sie ins Visier von US-Präsident Donald Trump.

spiegel.title: Hawaii: Hurrikan »Lala« zieht knapp vorbei
spiegel.description: Der tropische Sturm »Lala« hat sich zum Hurrikan verstärkt und ist dicht an Hawaiis Hauptinsel vorbeigezogen. Zehntausende sind ohne Strom, Straßen überflutet. Auch die Inseln Maui und Oahu müssen sich auf Sturm und Starkregen einstellen.

nzz.title: Unfall im Engadin: Polizei spricht vom schwersten Kutschenunglück der letzten Jahre
nzz.description: Bei einem Unfall mit einer Kutschenkomposition im Val Roseg kam am Samstag eine Person ums Leben. Zwölf weitere Personen wurden verletzt.

nzz.title: «Trete an, um zu gewinnen»: Valérie Dittli will trotz Widerstand der eigenen Partei erneut antreten
nzz.description: Die Waadtländer Staatsrätin gibt in einem Zeitungsinterview ihre Kandidatur bekannt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Migrantenansturm in Ceuta: Marokko nimmt Migranten vor Ceuta fest +++ Spanien führt Grenzkontrollen für Reisende aus Italien ein
nzz.description: Die Lage in der spanischen Exklave Ceuta in Nordafrika ist nach der Ankunft Tausender Migranten angespannt. Die neusten Meldungen zur Migrationskrise.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Erdbeben in Kolumbien: Zahl der Toten steigt auf rund 290
nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat am Montag Kolumbien erschüttert. Zahlreiche Gebäude stürzten ein und die Zahl der Verletzten könnte sich auf mehrere Hunderte belaufen. Die wichtigsten Antworten.

nzz.title: Ceuta bleibt dicht, doch die Krise ist nicht vorbei
nzz.description: Ein erneuter Ansturm auf die spanische Exklave blieb am Samstag aus. Die soziale Lage ist weiter dramatisch.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Libanon meldet Tote Angriffen im Süden des Landes​​​ +++ Trump will Strasse von Hormuz zu US-Territorium machen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Moskau meldet ukrainischen Drohnenangriff +++ Russischer Angriff tötet Baby
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Erdbeben der Stärke 7,7 in Indonesien: Opferzahl steigt erneut und liegt nun bei mindestens 51
nzz.description: Vor der indonesischen Insel Flores kommt es am Samstag zu einem sehr schweren Erdbeben. Zeitweise galt auch eine Tsunami-Warnung.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Vielleicht hilft bald nur noch der KI-Politberater
nzz.description: Die grossen Politthemen unserer Tage scheinen immer komplexer zu werden. Bisher konnte man sich als Stimmbürger immerhin an der Position seiner Lieblingspartei orientieren. Doch auch das wird immer schwieriger, wie derzeit die Europapolitik zeigt.

nzz.title: Die Beratungen um die neuen EU-Verträge beginnen mit einem Säbelrasseln
nzz.description: Aus dem Ständerat dringen widersprüchliche Signale. Der Streit um einen schärferen Kündigungsschutz für Arbeitnehmervertreter und eine rigide Kautionspflicht für europäische Unternehmen sollen die Abkommen mit Brüssel kippen.

nzz.title: Anlagebetrüger auf Social Media agieren immer dreister: Wie man fragwürdige Angebote zu Aktien, Finanzprodukten und Kryptowährungen erkennt
nzz.description: Dubiose Finanzmarktakteure setzen immer ausgeklügeltere Methoden ein, um Sparer auf ihre Plattformen zu locken. Bei folgenden Warnsignalen sollte man stutzig werden.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Donald Trump will den Zugang zu seinen Verlautbarungen verkaufen – und verrät damit die Ideale des amerikanischen Kapitalismus
nzz.description: In den USA setzt sich die zynische Haltung durch, dass gute Beziehungen und Insiderwissen eher zum Erfolg führen als harte Arbeit. Präsident Trump gibt den Zynikern recht.

nzz.title: Der TV-Fussballtrainer Ted Lasso ist jetzt nicht nur Everybody’s Darling, sondern auch Management-Guru
nzz.description: Ted Lassos unerschütterlicher Optimismus wird auf dieser Welt dringend gebraucht. Seine Herangehensweise findet nun sogar in Managementkursen Eingang.

nzz.title: Trotz Kriegen und Krisen: Die Löhne in der Schweiz werden nächstes Jahr steigen
nzz.description: Laut einer Umfrage der KOF können die Beschäftigten 2027 mit höheren Reallöhnen rechnen. Ob es tatsächlich so kommt, hängt von der künftigen Inflation ab. Ein Vergleich zeigt, in welchen Branchen die Gehälter am stärksten klettern.

nzz.title: Armer Roger Federer – jetzt schwimmt ihm das Geld davon
nzz.description: Der einst beste Tennisspieler der Welt ist nicht mehr Milliardär. Muss er jetzt das Geld wieder mit dem Racket verdienen?

nzz.title: Das Mekka-Abkommen macht den Nahen Osten weniger amerikanisch
nzz.description: Saudiarabien, Pakistan und die Türkei wollen ab sofort als Block auftreten. Die Interessen der Länder sind zwar verschieden, für Israel dürfte es dennoch ungemütlich werden.

observador.title: Fogo de Vinhais dominado este domingo de manhã
observador.description: Pelas 08h00 permaneciam no terreno, em Vinhais, 186 operacionais, apoiados por 71 viaturas. Fogo em Chaves (Vila Real) e Torre de Moncorvo (Bragança) lavravam ainda em "pequenas frentes".

observador.title: 8h. Incêndio em Chaves tem duas frentes ativas
observador.description: O comandante sub-regional do Alto Tâmega e Barroso disse à Rádio Observador que os trabalhos correram favoravelmente durante a noite. Ainda, Pedro Pichardo é vice-campeão europeu de triplo salto.

observador.title: 7h. MAI lamenta morte em acidente em Amarante
observador.description: Motociclista morreu depois de um acidente a envolver um camião dos bombeiros. Ainda, última etapa da Volta a Portugal vai hoje para a estrada.

observador.title: 6h. Ouvidas explosões em Kiev esta madrugada
observador.description: Administração militar reportou incêndio num edifício não residencial no distrito de Obolonsky. Ainda, Venezuela diz que foram libertados mais de mil presos políticos desde intervenção dos EUA.

observador.title: Que bateria dura mais tempo antes de ter de ser substituída?
observador.description: O tempo de vida útil das baterias é um dos motivos que leva muitos a não confiarem nos carros eléctricos. Estudo afirma que as melhores mantêm 95% de capacidade após 100.000 km.

observador.title: Diz-se "Argélia" ou "Algéria"? E usar "você" é má educação?
observador.description: Da influência do castelhano em "Argélia" à célebre expressão "você é de estrebaria", Marco Neves abre o "consultório de verão" do Português Suave para responder às dúvidas dos ouvintes.

observador.title: Pós-PRR, vamos andar de cheque em cheque? - Ouvintes
observador.description: No Fora do Baralho especial ouvintes, Nuno Garoupa responde a perguntas sobre o Plano de Recuperação e Resiliência (PRR), os erros cometidos e o que se espera quando terminar.

observador.title: 5h. PS faz rentrée em Olhão com críticas ao Governo
observador.description: José Luís Carneiro deve centrar discurso no custo de vida dos portugueses e nas críticas ao Governo. Ainda, ouvidas explosões em Kiev, depois de de ter sido acionado alerta de mísseis balísticos.

observador.title: 4h. Pedro Pichardo é vice-campeão europeu de triplo salto
observador.description: Atleta português conseguiu medalha de prata, depois de saltar 17,76 metros no primeiro ensaio. Ainda, OIM alerta para risco de tráfico de pessoas nas áreas afetadas pelo terramoto na Colômbia.

observador.title: 3h. Israel voltou a bombardear o sul do Líbano
observador.description: Acontecem depois de uma primeira ofensiva que matou 11 pessoas, incluindo crianças. Ainda, três incêndios no norte do país preocupam autoridades, no terreno estão cerca de 550 operacionais.

observador.title: 2h Três incêndios mobilizam cerca de 550 operacionais
observador.description: Fogo em Torre de Moncorvo, em Bragança, está a mobilizar mais meios, são 205 operacionais apoiados por 66 viaturas. Ainda, acidente com uma viatura dos bombeiros em Amarante provoca uma vítima mortal.

observador.title: 1h. Incêndio em Torre de Moncorvo mobiliza 175 operacionais
observador.description: Tem duas frentes ativas e está a ser combatido por 175 bombeiros e 58 viaturas. Não há  bens ou pessoas em perigo. Ainda, FC Porto vence Rio Ave, em Vila do Conde, e continua invicto no campeonato.

observador.title: Seguro quer fronteiras inseguras
observador.description: É assim que os nossos governantes, juizes e “activistas” de vária estirpe nos têm imposto os seus sobressaltos éticos que tornaram a Europa num caso único de desregramento e descontrolo.

observador.title: Rio Ave x Porto. "VAR anula bem o golo do Porto"
observador.description: Nota positiva para Miguel Fonseca na vitória do Porto em Vila do Conde. O árbitro "deixou jogar" e chegou a números "pouco habituais" na nossa liga: "apenas 12 faltas e 64 minutos de tempo útil."

observador.title: Senhoras conservadoras
observador.description: Que um conservador prefira distanciar-se disto a saudá-lo só tem um nome: pedantismo. Em última análise, trata-se de um almoço inofensivo cujo grande pecado é ser apenas um pouco ridículo.

observador.title: O Chega não tem nojo de mim
observador.description: A força dos evangélicos é não internalizarmos, como agora se diz em linguagem psico-emotiva, o nojo que sentem de nós. Venha esse nojo dos partidos políticos, da imprensa ou de qualquer outro lugar

observador.title: O Estado no papel e o cidadão à porta do Estado
observador.description: Mais do que novas leis ou plataformas digitais, a Administração Pública precisa de garantir que os direitos dos cidadãos existem também na realidade

observador.title: Liberalismo e conservadorismo
observador.description: Poderá o conservadorismo passar sem o liberalismo? Não. O conservador pouco ou nada tem a esperar do Estado. A tarefa de regeneração da sociedade civil cabe ao exercício das liberdades individuais.

phys-org.title: Nature has spent billions of years fighting bacteria. AI could help us learn its secrets
phys-org.description: Tiny viruses that infect bacteria could one day help us tackle infections that antibiotics can no longer treat. But first, scientists need to understand how these viruses work, and artificial intelligence could provide them with a powerful way to do that.

phys-org.title: How healthier farm animals can cut greenhouse gas emissions
phys-org.description: When a dairy cow miscarries, a farmer loses far more than an unborn calf. Feed has been grown, land and water have been used, and greenhouse gases have been released during the cow's pregnancy, but milk production, a future animal and income are lost.

phys-org.title: Exploring the moon will require rovers that can think for themselves
phys-org.description: NASA is planning to send three small rovers to the moon with a single instruction: Work out among yourselves how to explore a patch of ground.

phys-org.title: Topical clove oil for canine sarcoptic mange promises faster, plant-based treatment
phys-org.description: Canine sarcoptic mange (scabies) is a skin condition in which microscopic mites (Sarcoptes scabiei) infest dogs' skin. The condition is contagious and zoonotic and can be difficult to detect. If left untreated, it can cause bleeding sores, malnutrition, emaciation and secondary bacterial infections that may eventually lead to a dog's death.

phys-org.title: Early-universe plasma may have stopped dark photons from heating cosmos
phys-org.description: A new paper published in Physical Review Letters reveals that a leading dark matter candidate—the hypothetical "dark photon"—would not have heated the early universe as previously thought. The finding opens a vast region for experimental searches and could change the hunt for dark matter.

phys-org.title: Neptune's tiny moons tell the story of Triton's destructive capture
phys-org.description: Neptune's moon and ring system stand out among the giant planets because of the strange imbalance between its one very large moon and its many tiny moons. Its largest moon, Triton, makes up more than 99% of the mass of all satellites orbiting the planet while orbiting retrograde compared with Neptune's rotation. phys-org.title: One-off campus programs fall short on preventing sexual violence, review finds
phys-org.description: A recent National Student Safety Survey found that one in six students attending Australian universities had been sexually harassed and one in 20 had been sexually assaulted since starting university.

phys-org.title: Tungsten may suffer more radiation damage in fusion reactors than expected
phys-org.description: Fusion reactors, devices that generate energy by fusing light atomic nuclei at extremely high temperatures, could contribute to ongoing efforts aimed at producing electricity more sustainably. The extreme environment inside these devices, however, can damage materials that surround the superheated, electrically charged plasma where the nuclear fusion reaction takes place.

phys-org.title: Nonrepeating photonic crystal may enable more tunable, reliable semiconductor lasers
phys-org.description: Over the past two decades, photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers (PCSELs) have shown promise as a type of advanced semiconductor laser useful in defense- and aerospace-related applications. Typically, these devices are made with photonic crystal patterns that repeat across the area of the device. But new research from the lab of electrical and computer engineering professor Kent Choquette has demonstrated a quasi-periodic photonic-crystal surface-emitting laser (QPCSEL). phys-org.title: Minnesota iron ore could be key to sustainable and lower cost semiconductor
phys-org.description: For the first time, researchers at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities have demonstrated that the low-purity iron ore prevalent in Minnesota can be used to create semiconductor-quality iron sulfide, also known as "fool's gold" or pyrite. This discovery could have cost-effective and sustainable applications in future electronic devices and other technologies.

phys-org.title: Four more belugas arrive at Chicago aquarium from shuttered Canadian theme park
phys-org.description: Four more belugas have arrived at a Chicago aquarium as part of a plan to move Canada's last remaining captive whales from a shuttered theme park to aquariums in the United States and Spain.

phys-org.title: Shackled men in 2,600-year-old Greek mass graves were likely locals, archaeologists find
phys-org.description: In 2016, archaeologists working at the Phaleron Burial Ground, part of the ancient Attica region, uncovered an astonishing sight: three mass graves dating to the 7th and 6th centuries BCE containing the skeletons of 79 adult men. Many were bound together with metal shackles.

phys-org.title: Scientists simulating ant swarms find a 'first mover' can set the colony in motion
phys-org.description: In ant colonies, a single ant can be the catalyst for a wave of mob activity, launching brief bursts of coordinated movement involving hundreds or even thousands of swarming workers, according to new simulations from New Jersey Institute of Technology.

phys-org.title: Black-box technologies could undermine confidence in scientific findings
phys-org.description: Scientists are increasingly relying on powerful data sources and tools that they often cannot fully understand, inspect or verify, according to a new study.

phys-org.title: Hurricane poised to hit Hawaii as El Niño stirs Pacific
phys-org.description: A strengthening tropical storm named Lala is set to hit Hawaii's Big Island with hurricane-force gales on Saturday, bringing dangerous winds, rainfall and heavy surf.

phys-org.title: Extreme weather is making work difficult for many people. This is what needs to change
phys-org.description: The UK has experienced several heat waves this summer—heat stress among workers is one of the biggest causes of weather-related sick leave. Very high temperatures can cause symptoms like heat rash and cramps, or even exhaustion and heatstroke.

phys-org.title: Faced with historic drought, the Dutch rethink water management
phys-org.description: On the banks of the Waal, the Dutch branch of the Rhine, swimmers are sunning themselves on a Nijmegen beach that didn't exist before the river level dropped a few months ago.

phys-org.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off coast of Indonesia and tsunami warning issued
phys-org.description: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early Saturday, damaging buildings and homes, and triggering a tsunami warning. Authorities urged people on affected coastlines to move to higher ground.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

crunchbase.title: AI-Native, Not AI-Sprinkle: Why AI Is A Business Change, Not A Technology Change
crunchbase.description: Companies unlock AI’s biggest productivity gains not by adding AI tools to existing workflows, but by redesigning teams, roles and daily work around AI. crunchbase.title: The Biggest Consequence Of An AI IPO Isn’t The IPO Itself. It’s What Happens Afterward.
crunchbase.description: A wave of major AI IPOs could return significant liquidity to limited partners, fueling a new venture fundraising cycle rather than simply affecting public-market valuations.
